newsitem.title: UK: Stg steadies above 2.78 marks, eye on France.
newsitem.headline: Stg steadies above 2.78 marks, eye on France.

text.p: Sterling steadied just above 2.78 marks at midday in Europe after an early stumble lower after the mark, alert to a possible snap general election in France, moved higher.
Mounting speculation of a snap French election dragged the franc and its European partners down against the mark as it prompted a fresh bout of nerves about European monetary union (EMU).
"The impact on sterling/mark has followed mark buying in Europe," said Philippe Delmotte from Bank of Boston's corporate sales department.
The prospect of an early French poll has sparked concern in markets that power could pass to a Socialist-led alliance which might struggle to reconcile pro-EMU policies with efforts to boost growth.
French President Jacques Chirac will make a broadcast to the nation on Monday at 1800 GMT, his office said.

"If (French President Jacques) Chirac dissolves parliament, we are looking for mark/French franc to gain further," said Delmotte. At 0943 GMT stg/mark was trading at 2.7830/40 against 2.7959/64 in late Europe on Friday and just above two-week lows of 2.7780 marks hit in early dealing.
Against the French franc, the mark stood at 3.3717/22 at midday in Europe against 3.3694/99 in late Europe on Friday.
"On sterling, most of the action has now died down," said a trader at a UK bank, adding that the focus was on France and the possibility of a snap election there.
Technically, however, he said sterling would be vulnerable to a re-test of two-week lows around 2.7780 marks hit earlier.
"There is still room on the downside to test the 2.7720/30 marks area before we see a bounce," he said.
Cable was firm at midday in Europe, though just off session peaks at $1.6383 hit earlier, riding higher on a weaker dollar.
At 1022 GMT cable was off its peak and trading at $1.6332/42, against $1.6312/22 in late Europe on Friday, as the dollar steadied against the mark in Europe.
"Cable is very well bid at $1.6310, so it is unlikely to slip much beyond there," said the UK bank dealer.
Currency markets were also generally cautious ahead of the April 27 weekend meeting of G7 finance ministers in Washington.
Analysts said the issue of the strong dollar against the yen is likely to be a focus of the meeting, with the risk of a strongly worded statement.
